captions.detailed: A classic city upright bicycle front fork and handlebar assembly. It features a dark-colored fork with a vertical steerer tube and two tapered blade legs. A tall, light-grey stem is mounted to the steerer tube via a dual-clamp revolute joint, allowing the stem to rotate or fold forward. At the top of the stem, a swept-back black handlebar with cylindrical hand grips is secured in a clamp, allowing rotational adjustment on another revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a city upright bicycle fork and handlebar assembly. The model should include a dark-colored fork with tapered legs, a light-grey tall stem that articulates on a revolute joint at the steerer tube, and a swept-back black handlebar with grips that can rotate relative to the stem clamp.
captions.factory: Construct the fork using a Cylinder for the steerer tube, a Box for the crown, and two tapered cylinders or extruded profiles for the blade legs. Model the tall stem using a series of boxes and cylinders to form the lower clamp, the main angled neck, and the upper handlebar clamp. Create the handlebar using an extruded path or swept profile for the swept-back wings, capped with cylinders for the hand grips. Define two revolute joints: one connecting the stem base to the fork steerer, and one connecting the handlebar center to the stem's upper clamp.
